title: The autopilot detects stalled or hampered work and works through a ladder of remedies
goal: backlog.py stalled lists each claimed or ready item with its stall signals read from claims, git and the ops rows (a claim with no commit past a limit, a refused done repeated, a check that timed out twice, land stopping at the same step twice, a red main, a host lock wait past a limit, a worker that returned without a commit); kb-sprint names the remedy ladder for each signal (retry once narrower, release and redispatch with the failure named in the brief, file the blocker as a bug or story and take the next ready item, ask the operator through a gate or the digest); the autopilot never idles while a ready item remains, and each remedy it takes leaves an ops row and an autopilot decision.

gates.question: This adds a mechanism before a failure it answers has happened (backlog.md, Changing this process). Add it anyway?

notes: It reads claims and git with held and horizon, which exist; the stall limits are named in the work, not guessed here.
